title: Leveraging Large Language Models for NLG Evaluation: Advances and Challenges

bias_targets.methodology: Literature review of studies demonstrating that LLM evaluators show a preference for options based on their sequence or position in the prompt.
Literature review of studies revealing that LLM evaluators exhibit a tendency to favor and assign higher scores to texts generated by themselves compared to other models.
Literature review of findings that LLMs acting as judges systematically prefer longer or shorter texts regardless of actual quality.

Discussion of how stereotypes related to specific demographic identities (e.g., race, gender, religion, culture, and ideology) carry over from a model's generation capabilities into its evaluative role.
